gp.text: Gross profit . As a result of the foregoing, our total gross profit decreased by $872,820, or 45.71%, to $1,036,759 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $1,909,579 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Our total gross margin (as a percentage of revenue) decreased from 62.43% for the three months ended September 30, 2025 to 54.22% for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

cor.text: Management uses revenues, cost of sales, operating expenses, and income (loss) before taxes to evaluate and measure its subsidiaries’ success. To help the segments achieve optimal operating performance, management retains the prior owners of the subsidiaries and allows them to do what they do best, which is run the business. Additionally, management monitors key metrics primarily revenues and income from operations in order to allocate resources accordingly.

ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses . Our selling, general and administrative expenses consist primarily of accounting, auditing, legal and public reporting expenses, personnel expenses, including employee salaries and bonuses plus related payroll taxes, professional advisor fees, credit losses, rent expense, insurance and other expenses incurred in connection with general operations. Our selling, general and administrative expenses decreased by $21,139, or 1.73%, to $1,203,211 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $1,224,350 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. As a percentage of revenue, our selling, general and administrative expenses were 62.92% and 40.03% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily attributable to decreases in professional fees, rent and general administration and office costs, offset by increases in the allowance for credit loss, billing costs and payroll related costs.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses . Our selling, general and administrative expenses consist primarily of accounting, auditing, legal and public reporting expenses, personnel expenses, including employee salaries and bonuses plus related payroll taxes, professional advisor fees, credit losses, rent expense, insurance and other expenses incurred in connection with general operations. Our selling, general and administrative expenses decreased by $21,139, or 1.73%, to $1,203,211 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $1,224,350 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. As a percentage of revenue, our selling, general and administrative expenses were 62.92% and 40.03% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in selling, general and administrative expenses was primarily attributable to decreases in professional fees, rent and general administration and office costs, offset by increases in the allowance for credit loss, billing costs and payroll related costs.

net.text: Net loss . As a result of the cumulative effect of the factors described above, our net loss was $3,206,551 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $1,144,299 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase in loss of $2,062,252, or 180.22%.

ocf.text: Our net cash used in operating activities was $235,975 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $2,463,300 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The primary drivers of our net cash used in operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 are our net loss of $8,777,531 and an increase of $1,409,255 in accounts receivable, offset by an increase of $6,524,189 in interest expense included in the line of credit, the loss on issuance or change in value of the derivative liability of $493,014, stock compensation expense or shares issued for services rendered of $1,401,116, an increase of $207,097 in accounts payable and other accrued expenses, an increase in accrued interest of $273,494, and an increase in accrued related parties compensation expense of $939,729. For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, the primary drivers of our net cash used in operating activities were our net loss of $2,821,471 and an increase of $4,878,236 in accounts receivable, offset by an increase of $4,292,471 in interest expense included in the line of credit balance.

da.text: Depreciation expense . Our depreciation expense was $233, or 0.01% of revenue, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $762, or 0.02% of revenue, for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

sbc.text: Share-based compensation expense . Share-based compensation expense was $369,981 and $41,188 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Share-based compensation expense in both 2026 and 2025 consisted of expense related to the issuance of common stock to our board of directors, officers and employees, our investor relations firm and other consultants for services provided.

capex.text: We have no off-balance sheet arrangements that have or are reasonably likely to have a current or future effect on our financial condition, changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
